plantedOcclusionStudy.attributionBoundary: The DOM failure made an incomplete child-only stacking repair that DOM preview falsely accepted. Generic screenshot narration exposed the still-empty control and caused the missing parent repair. Both task-aware runs repaired source before preview, so their strict passes prove non-regression and efficiency, not a task-aware intervention.

taskAwareFollowUp.boundary: The review-first intervention now supplies direct full-agent attribution: DOM-only failed 0/4 while task-aware review emitted four initial REPAIR verdicts, caused four repairs, then emitted eight CLEAR verdicts and passed 4/4 across Terra and Sol. An already-correct paired cohort passed 4/4 in both DOM and task-aware arms with zero edits, but vision added requests, tokens, and latency. This supports structured review inside the explicit vision opt-in, not global default-on vision.

candidates.reason: The earlier broad-suite generic pass gain was not causally attributable. The new review-first study supplies causal target evidence across Terra and Sol, and the paired clear cohort shows no false repairs, but task-aware vision still adds material request, token, and latency cost on already-correct pages. Keep screenshot vision globally opt-in while preferring the more efficient structured task-aware protocol inside that opt-in.

Structured REPAIR/CLEAR output is now trusted preview proof instead of unbound prose. On the causal target it matched generic vision correctness while saving five turns per model and 5–6 requests; on the clear control it made no edits. The enclosing screenshot capability remains default-off because its non-target cost is material.

Chromium elementFromPoint evidence closes a measured DOM-preview false green without a vision request. It produced 4/4 causal repairs versus 0/4 with the detector disabled, stayed silent and edit-free on 4/4 already-correct controls, caught an incomplete child-only z-index repair, and was cheaper than task-aware screenshot review for both Terra and Sol.

candidates.reason: The optional screenshot process cannot prove a fault in an already-completed DOM interaction process. Separating the phase evidence removes the preserved Terra false attribution while deterministic negative controls keep real and legacy interaction timeouts blocking.

The operator-only calibration command measures screenshot-review sensitivity and false interventions without running a coding agent. Its final evidence is self-contained and independently reconstructs the archived contract, derived task-aware prompt hashes, screenshot bytes, verdicts, matrix completeness, and aggregate scores.

The prior two-minute idle deadline killed valid workers; generation-sized deadlines completed both live Terra and Sol batches, while injected all-failed and partially-failed cases now produce distinct terminal and partial outcomes.
The detector closes a false-green offline-preview gap and the focused Terra/Sol regression passed 2/2.

Whole-page word matching treated ordinary campaign prose as a keyboard contract and induced unrelated code. Detection now requires an explicit P-to-pause instruction or a visible pause/resume control; a deterministic negative control closes the observed regression while the positive control preserves the intended game defect check.
Per-source accounting is additive and behavior-neutral; a fresh strict pass proved exact reconciliation through the run artifact, experiment manifest, and Markdown summary.

The packet adds deterministic provenance and an offline visual comparison surface without another model call; unit Chromium rendering passed and the live two-image self-critique remained strict-green.

A complete scripted fixture lifecycle proved that managed generated evidence survives isolated workspace cleanup and remains directly renderable, while bounded no-follow copying prevents uncontrolled or external-file capture.
The live two-variant run had a 2.2-minute quiet window. Event-only heartbeats make progress visible in interactive and experiment output without another model call or prompt change.
Structured provenance separates user intent from infrastructure behavior, preventing cancellation from being misdiagnosed as provider instability or a generic generation failure.
All routed tools now cross one registry-owned evidence boundary; legacy image and preview shapes remain compatible while agent control flow and artifacts consume only the normalized envelope.
Axis and quality concepts accept visually equivalent language without weakening the image-specific policy; this removes known semantic false negatives while retaining negative controls.

A read-only, model-free command now independently checks the evidence BANTAM uses to make improvement claims. It changes no agent policy, treats legacy absence as explicit non-applicability, and fails present evidence on byte, path, schema, count, arithmetic, final-diff, or prompt-integrity disagreement.

External vision and image-generation cost now remains attached to the exact tool turn that caused it, and the independent auditor reconciles those envelopes with run-level source accounting. The identical live fixture retained strict correctness, turns, and requests while replacing an unprovable null linkage with exact evidence.

Fixture and experiment success now requires both task correctness and a valid complete evidence envelope. The audit runs after attachments and final diff are assembled but before acceptance, so a green verifier cannot launder malformed proof.

Replay A/B is an explicit operator tool, not an agent default. It reconstructs the recorded runtime, rotates baseline-first and candidate-first call position when multiple samples exist, labels single-order evidence honestly, persists exact order plus per-arm provider usage and latency, SHA-256 binds each new arm's request/output/usage/timing/error receipt to its sample and position, independently reconstructs each request hash and fidelity from the source artifact and remedy, requires optional edit applicability to the recorded prompt, stores relocatable hash-linked evidence, and self-audits before publication.

candidates.reason: The miner turns the existing evidence corpus into bounded exact-task, evaluator-compatible specimen discovery without another model call. New runs persist exact task-spec, starting-repository, and grader roots; legacy comparisons are conservatively limited to one experiment. This removed a demonstrated cross-experiment grader-drift false cohort and 13 unsupported failure references while preserving same-experiment tournament evidence. It indexes prior studies only by immutable artifact hash plus exact turn, retains every compatible candidate, and explicitly refuses to infer audit validity, a shared cause, a remedy, or promotion.

candidates.reason: The paired transaction closes the measured shell escape left by direct edit refusal alone: immutable direct edits are rejected, protected shell mutations are restored, misleading green output is invalidated, and allowed source changes survive. A same-trajectory control proves cheated-to-pass recovery and Terra/Sol show no behavioral regression when the mechanism is inactive, but the native study contains no natural intervention and one fixture is not enough to change evaluation defaults.

It now uses the same runtime-aware resolver as the development launcher; a preserved failed batch proves the before state and the fresh four-run native study proves the repaired path.
